title: bucketized-kv-slab-sharding-and-transactional-pin-optimizer
author: Aisha Banerjee
release_notes: Improves KV cache throughput and tail latency by introducing bucketized slab sharding and a transactional pin API; reduces fragmentation and speeds up eviction decisions. No API surface changes for external users of the public inference API.
description:
Motivation: Our paged KV cache shows suboptimal reuse under high-concurrency multi-model workloads, and background reclamation contends on a single global allocator lock which amplifies tail latency. This PR introduces a bucketized slab sharding strategy plus a lightweight transactional pin API to group pin/unpin operations across request lifecycles and reduce global contention.
Summary of changes: 1) New bucketized slab allocator: splits the block arena into N runtime-controllable buckets driven by model-hint and size-class histograms; each bucket has its own freelist/eviction-heap and background reclaim worker to avoid hot global locks. 2) Transactional pin API: pins can be grouped into a short-lived transaction object that commits or aborts atomically, allowing the allocator to coalesce pin metadata updates and defer non-critical refcount churn. 3) Cross-bucket eviction hints: scheduler emits soft-affinity hints so long-lived KV entries are preferentially kept on the bucket matching their access pattern; eviction workers consult a small bloom+LRU sketch to prioritize candidates. 4) Adaptive reuse heuristics: block reuse now considers recent prefix-KV access and request latency SLOs to favor low-latency reuse versus aggressive compaction. 5) Observability: added per-bucket counters (allocs, evicts, contention-ms), per-transaction histograms, and a new dashboard panel. 6) Kernel/fastpath: optimized hot-copy path with 64B vectorized memcpy fallback using architecture-specific intrinsics for x86_64 and a plain memcpy for other arches.

Files changed (high level): - src/kv/allocator/bucketed_allocator.{cc,h} - src/kv/allocator/transactional_pin.{cc,h} - src/kv/evict/evict_worker.cc - src/kv/fastpath/memcopy_optim.{cc} - tests/kv/allocator_tests.cc - perf/bench/kv_bucket_shard_bench.py - docs/kv/transactional_pin.md - observability/dashboards/kv_buckets.json
Review conversation summary: - Marcus Li: Requested clearer invariants for cross-bucket pin transfers; asked for explicit ordering guarantees on commit to avoid ABA on refcounts. Author reply: added strong atomic commit with sequence tokens and unit tests covering concurrent commit/abort scenarios. - Priya Nair: Noted potential memory blowup if transaction abort path leaks temporary pins; requested a stress test. Author reply: implemented scoped-guard and added stress test with abort/no-op scenarios; CI stress run attached. - Evan Ortiz: Asked for perf numbers vs existing allocator under 4000 concurrent connections and mixed model load. Author reply: included perf-canary outputs showing 18% throughput uplift and 24% tail latency reduction p95->p99 compared to main under matched hardware.
CI and checks: - Build: pass - Unit tests: pass - Integration (perf-canary): pass - Lint: pass - Security scan: pass
Merge outcome: approved by reviewers and merged via squash-and-merge after green CI.
Notes on rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag kv.bucket_sharding.enabled=false by default for canary rollout; knob kv.bucket_count default=4; operator docs provided for Dedicated/Private deploys.
Backwards compatibility: allocator change is internal; on-disk KV layout unchanged.
Observability/alerts: added alert kv_bucket_reclaim_latency_ms > 2000ms for 5m.
Follow-ups: - ENG-2801: auto-tune kv.bucket_count based on workload distribution (tracked) - Consider exposing transactional pin tracing spans in Console for deep debugging.
